A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoGeo research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, weather-robustness evaluations, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds concept-router weight visualizations and training-set mutual-information measurements.

M1.justification: The CACS, CSRR, OCVA, and relational-distillation components, their losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged. The newly specified slot-refinement iteration counts in Appendix C.1 disclose implementation details without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate University-1652, SUES-200, DenseUAV, and GTA-V, retaining the same transfer directions, altitude coverage, and weather scenarios. GTA-V cross-area evaluation already appears in v1. The new diagnostics reuse existing training datasets.

E2.justification: The retrieval and computational-cost comparator sets remain unchanged. The new Appendix B.2 analysis adds a limited diagnostic comparison between conditional mutual information in pretrained DINOv2 features and trained InfoGeo features. Newly cited localization methods are not added to the retrieval comparisons.

E3.justification: One benchmark's reported settings are revised: GTA-V training drone/satellite counts change from 25,200/8,400 to 15,693/14,640, and testing counts from 33,763/14,640 to 18,070/14,640 (v1 Table 7; v5 Table 8). This does not establish that experiments were rerun. v5 also introduces training-set MI diagnostics; existing retrieval metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 Figure 5 adds query/gallery router-weight visualizations with and without Lcacs, examining its effect on concept selection. Appendix B.2 and Table 7 add an empirical check of conditional independence using mutual information. Existing component ablations, sensitivity studies, weather tests, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures. v5 adds MI point estimates and describes dependence as statistically insignificant, but supplies no corresponding uncertainty estimate or testing procedure.

E6.justification: Matched retrieval, ablation, and computational-cost table values remain unchanged. New Table 7 reports unconditional MI of 0.3472, 0.0797, and 0.1540, with conditional MI reported as 0.0000; Figure 5 adds weight-polarization findings. Section 5.4 also newly claims a 1.5% average AP gain from distillation, although unchanged Table 5 implies approximately 1.09 percentage points.

T1.justification: The information-bottleneck objectives, conditional-independence assumption, bounds, and substantive derivations are retained. The additional Markov-chain equation in Appendix B.2 repeats an existing formulation. The new empirical analysis does not introduce a new theorem, assumption, or corrected proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: object-centric CVGL, an information-bottleneck formulation, and improved generalization and weather robustness across four benchmarks. Wording changes do not materially alter these claims.

C2.justification: v5 interprets its new router plots as evidence of polarized, view-dependent concept selection and its near-zero conditional MI as empirical validation of conditional independence and the Markov formulation. Existing limitations concerning altitude, noisy object relations, slot collapse, and retrieval failures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies three refinement iterations for unconditional queries and one for conditional queries, and replaces the BO-QSA attribution to Gould et al. with Jia et al. Existing hardware, optimizer, network dimensions, training budgets, and warm-up settings are retained; no code or data-access resource is added.

R1.justification: v5 adds references including Jia et al., Kipf et al., JRN-Geo, MRGeo, and causal/geometric-topology CVGL, while removing Gould et al. and the panorama-BEV co-retrieval reference. Related-work discussion receives limited updates, including emphasis on 3D structural alignment. The overall novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized paragraph rewrites, clarifies explanations of routing and distillation, corrects author-name and terminology errors, and adds an acknowledgement. The main section sequence and Appendix A–E organization remain intact; this is not a wholesale narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v5 adds the router-weight Figure 5 and MI Table 7, redraws the existing sensitivity figure, and relocates several retained figures and tables. Captions and dataset-table labels are refined, and the placeholder running header is replaced with the paper title. The overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: v5 offers limited gains in reproducibility and clarity through explicit refinement counts, improved attribution, and direct visualization of router behavior. The method and retrieval evidence remain stable. These gains are partly offset by the new AP-summary inconsistency and underdocumented MI measurements, whose significance language is unsupported by a stated test. The unexplained GTA-V count revisions also leave uncertainty about the reported experimental setting, so the revision does not establish a substantial improvement in scientific validation.
